clinical_category: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control

semantic_correction.stem: A client has a documented natural-rubber latex allergy. Which examination glove should the nurse select for direct care?

options.A: A nitrile examination glove made without natural-rubber latex.
options.B: A powder-free examination glove made from natural-rubber latex.
options.C: A natural-rubber latex glove worn over a thin cotton glove liner.
options.D: Two layers of natural-rubber latex examination gloves for added protection.

semantic_correction.rationale: FDA guidance states that if a healthcare worker or patient is allergic to natural-rubber latex, medical gloves made from other synthetic materials such as nitrile, PVC, or polyurethane should be chosen. A nitrile examination glove therefore avoids the allergen identified in the stem. Powder-free status, glove liners, or double gloving do not change the fact that the other options still contain natural-rubber latex.
semantic_correction.educational_objective: For a client with natural-rubber latex allergy, select a synthetic non-latex medical glove such as nitrile rather than a natural-rubber latex glove.
semantic_correction.source_version_date: Current FDA medical-device guidance page accessed August 21, 2026
semantic_correction.source_locator: What you should know before using medical gloves — natural-rubber latex allergy: choose gloves made from other synthetic materials such as PVC, nitrile, or polyurethane
semantic_correction.source_claim_supported: FDA advises choosing medical gloves made from synthetic non-latex materials such as nitrile, PVC, or polyurethane when the patient or healthcare worker is allergic to natural-rubber latex.

semantic_correction.correction_summary_append: RULE1 cleanup: retained the FDA-supported latex-allergy construct, removed the absolute-word distractor, rebuilt all alternatives as realistic glove-selection choices, and mapped the item to the explicit NCSBN allergy and infection-prevention activity statements.

audit_findings_append.source_locator: Medical Gloves — What you should know before using medical gloves
audit_findings_append.blueprint_locator: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control, printed pp. 24 and 26
audit_findings_append.finding: The original item was clinically correct but one distractor used an obvious absolute. The revised options compare actual glove-selection strategies; only the nitrile option removes natural-rubber latex exposure.

option_audit.A: Correct. Nitrile is one of the synthetic non-latex glove materials specifically identified by FDA for latex-allergic patients or workers.
option_audit.B: Incorrect. Powder-free natural-rubber latex still contains the allergenic material identified in the stem.
option_audit.C: Incorrect. A liner does not remove exposure to the natural-rubber latex glove material.
option_audit.D: Incorrect. Double gloving with natural-rubber latex increases layers but does not eliminate latex exposure.

ambiguity_check: No second defensible answer. A is the only option made from a synthetic non-latex material; B, C, and D all retain natural-rubber latex.
cueing_check: All four choices are concrete glove-selection strategies of comparable length and syntax; no absolute-word or unique-length cue identifies A.
